resolutions.note: The reader was right: a gas takes the shape of its container too, so the stem admitted two answers and punished a child who had just learned that gases fill their containers. The property that actually picks out a liquid is fixed volume, which the old stem never mentioned. Rewritten to "Which state of matter pours into a cup and takes its shape?" — pouring into a cup is fixed volume in words a grade-2 child already has.
